meeting_header:
Date: 2026-09-30
Start Time (UTC): 20:00
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Ramesh, Luca Chen, Jordan Patel (Redwood) — Priya Mehta, Evan Ortiz, Sofia Park, Alan Bishop (Harmonic Health)
summary: Kickoff to scope a POC focused on workload "traffic signature" and benchmark design. Confirmed success criteria (99th percentile inference latency < 450ms for 90% of requests, functional parity with current model, cost target <$0.0008/token), data sharing plan (72h logs), security constraints (VPC peering, KMS, SOC2 evidence), and timeline for bench runs and SOW. Action items and next steps assigned.
topics: Input/output token distribution and prompt pools
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE, nice to meet Harmonic Health team. we're running on a tight window so we'll focus on traffic signature and the bench design.
[00:18] Priya: hi Maya, thanks. we pulled in Evan and Sofia and alan for security bits. we want to validate both latency and cost for our triage assistant use case.
[00:32] Luca: quick intros — Luca, infra SE. i'll lead the replay and benchmarks side. Jordan on the call as well for ops questions.
[00:47] Evan: hey. small note, our infra is GCP, VPC peering is doable, want to confirm KMS and audit log requirements up front.
[01:05] Maya: perfect, we work with GCP peering, and we can integrate customer-managed KMS; we'll share the SOC 2 + ISO docs.
[01:22] Priya: high level — our volume today is bursty. average qps around 8 but peaks to 240 in short windows, concurrency per model is the big unknown for us. tail latency is killing the user experience.
[01:40] Luca: that burst shape is super helpful. when you say peaks to 240, is that sustained for minutes or seconds?
[01:48] Priya: usually seconds, like 10–40s bursts, sometimes a couple minutes during shift changes. distribution skew is heavy — 10% of requests are long-context followups with 800+ input tokens.
[02:06] Jordan: also many short prompts, single-sentence prompts, like confirmation or quick clarifications. output tokens vary a lot.
[02:18] Maya: ok so for the POC we'll need a token mix: short prompts (<=40 input tokens, <=80 output tokens) make up ~70%, medium prompts (40–200 inputs, 200–600 outputs) ~20%, and long-context prompts (600–1200 inputs, 400–1000 outputs) ~10% — is that roughly accurate?
[02:40] Priya: yes that's a good approximation.
[02:47] Sofia: our success criteria — user-facing response under 400ms p50 and p95 under 350ms? wait that doesn't make sense — we mean p50 under 200ms, p95 under 400ms, p99 under 700ms for the triage quick path. but for long context we can tolerate higher tails.
[03:10] Maya: good, we'll capture two SLA bands: quick-path and long-session. recommend POC KPIs: p50, p95, p99 latency, token cost per request, functional parity measured by eval set (we'll take a small human-checked sample), and no PII leakage.
[03:36] Evan: about cost — we need a rough ballpark to compare to our in-house infra. target is <$0.0008 per token overall. can we get that?
[03:48] Luca: depends a lot on batching and KV cache hit rates. with prefix caching and workload-aware batching we've seen 30–60% effective token cost reduction on similar mixes. We'll instrument replay to show cache-effective tokens.
[04:06] Priya: walk me through the replay plan. we can't share raw PII logs, so we'll anonymize — do you accept hashed user ids and masked free text?
[04:18] Maya: yes, hashed ids and masked text is fine. for the replay we prefer JSONL with timestamp, prompt, response length, model metadata. share 72 hours and mark production peak windows.
[04:33] Jordan: is live traffic mirroring in scope for the POC?
[04:38] Luca: for initial bench we do offline replay. If you want live mirroring later, that's an add-on and we evaluate fallthroughs and A/B. but not needed for phase 1.
[04:52] Priya: timeline check — we want pilot results in three weeks if possible. is that realistic?
[04:58] Maya: tight but possible. day 0–3 docs and SOW, day 3–9 log ingestion and replay setup, day 10–14 initial runs, day 15–21 iteration and run final bench, results and recommendation end of week 3.
[05:18] Alan: security items — we require customer-managed KMS, dedicated audit logs to our SIEM, RBAC mapped to our IdP (SAML), and minimal data-at-rest retention for logs. Also need to confirm where inference artifacts are stored.
[05:38] Luca: we can use your KMS for key wrapping, and audit logs are exported via logging sink; RBAC and SAML we support. we'll need to confirm HSM requirement — is HSM mandatory or KMS okay?
[05:54] Alan: KMS is fine for pilot, HSM preferred for production but we can defer. Also need SOC2 docs and a checklist.
[06:06] Maya: we'll attach SOC2 report and our security whitepaper.
[06:12] Priya: back to workload — concurrency is the hard part. we don't know how many concurrent sessions will probe the long-context model. can we profile a concurrency curve?
[06:24] Luca: yes, replay can simulate concurrency by preserving inter-arrival times and using ramp scripts. we also do synthetic bursts to stress tail. We'll produce concurrency vs p99 graphs.
[06:38] Priya: what about model variants — we use a large model for long-context but prefer a trimmed quantized variant for quick-paths. can Redwood route to different model sizes automatically?
[06:50] Maya: yes, smart routing and model variants are part of Redwood — we can configure policy to route short prompts to a cheaper quantized model and fallback to the large model for long context. That will factor into cost calculations.
[07:06] Evan: curious about KV cache — if we have repeated prefixes in followups, how does that impact tokens billed?
[07:14] Luca: KV caching reduces compute for the cached prefix — depends on hit rate; replay will estimate effective cache hits. We'll also instrument tokenized lengths and effective tokens per step. sometimes transcripts show 'K V cache' in logs which confuses tokenizers so we might need sample normalization.
[07:36] Priya: we have a concern: can the replay handle obfuscated tokens or mixed languages? Many of our prompts include Spanish phrases.
[07:44] Jordan: our replay is language-agnostic because it replays token sequences; the tokenizer can handle unicode. we should provide a sample so we can sanity check.
[07:57] Sofia: benchmark metrics — please include throughput per GPU, latency distribution, and cost per 1M tokens extrapolated. also show sensitivity to batch size and sequence length.
[08:10] Luca: will do. we'll produce a bench report with charts: qps vs p95/p99, cost curves, and recommended quantization profiles.
[08:22] Priya: okay — for success criteria final — we propose: p95 quick-path <= 400ms, p99 quick-path <= 700ms, cost <= $0.0008/token, functional parity (BLEU-ish? no, human eval pass rate >= 95% on reduced set).
[08:39] Maya: we captured that. We'll add toggle for RU (recall/use-case) and human eval threshold.
[08:45] Alan: side question — data residency: logs can stay in our project. Are there any copies retained by Redwood during bench?
[08:53] Maya: for the replay we ingest into ephemeral storage in your VPC or peered storage; Redwood does not retain raw text beyond the pilot window unless you opt-in. We'll put that in SOW.
[09:06] Priya: good. about the bench harness — can you share a sample docker image or helm chart? we prefer reproducible infra.
[09:15] Luca: yes we'll share a dockerfile, a small helm chart for test harness, and a sample replay script (python). Link we'll post in follow-up: LINK: https://redwood.example/poc-harmonic-harness (placeholder).
[09:35] Sofia: curious on metrics collection — do you instrument token-level cost or just per-request?
[09:41] Luca: both. we'll report raw tokens, effective tokens after cache, and compute ms per token. we'll also export traces for p99 debug.
[09:52] Priya: any limitations on model family? we use an Open weights model today with custom adapter layers — can Redwood serve it?
[09:59] Maya: we onboard custom models; need model artifact format and possibly conversion step. we can handle common weights formats but may need a quick model onboarding call.
[10:12] Jordan: that onboarding usually takes 2–4 days for conversions, can be parallel to replay prep.
[10:20] Evan: network egress costs — when you show cost per token do you factor in cross-region egress?
[10:27] Luca: benchmark cost is compute + infra; we'll annotate egress and storage. for fairness we'll show cost both with and without egress.
[10:36] Priya: excellent. ok i want to flag one more: error modes — sometimes long-context requests hit memory OOM with certain quantized configs. will benchs detect that?
[10:47] Luca: yes we'll include stability run with longer sequences to surface OOMs and tail failures. We'll include error-rate and fallback behavior.
[10:57] Maya: recap: Redwood to send SOW + security package, Luca to share harness, Harmonic to deliver 72h logs + prompt pools, target bench week mid-Oct and results by end of week three.
[11:15] Priya: thanks — can you also include a short checklist for what we need server-side to enable peering?
[11:20] Maya: yes checklist will be included in the SOW email.
[11:25] Alan: i'll review KMS permissions once i see the draft.
[11:28] Sofia: one last thing — can you show a short example of routing policy config? just pseudo-yaml so our platform folks can see how routing is declared.
[11:36] Jordan: we have a sample routing policy in the playbook we'll attach.
[11:40] Maya: ok wrapping up. thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links and dates.
[11:46] Priya: great, appreciate it.
[11:48] (call ends)

Notes: Transcript has occasional mis-transcriptions e.g., 'K V cache' vs 'KV cache', 'prefix caching' sometimes heard as 'pre-fix caching'. references to the harness link are placeholders and will be replaced in follow-up email.
